text:
julie: Heads up — noticed after the console gate roll (per-route quota UI) some client requests lost route metadata and are hitting the tenant default quota. Is that expected? CC @aj
aj: hmm, which SDKs? any logs? :thinking_face:
julie: python + ts so far. Support logs show the client sends `x-rd-route` but when we flip `console.strict_route_attrs` the header disappears on the proxy side. example we see in support: `request.headers['x-rd-route']` is null for ~2% of calls.
kevin: ah — that's the normalization rewrite I pushed yesterday. It was supposed to drop unknown attrs to reduce noisy dashboard lines. sounds like it dropped everything when the schema mismatch happened. investigating.
samir: for context, the flag was toggled during canary 6101020000 by deploy-bot and we didn't coordinate an SDK opt-in. customers on older SDK versions were affected.
maria: this is breaking. proposal: 1) add a proxy shim that preserves unknown route attrs into `x-rd-route-raw` 2) add an SDK opt-in header `x-rd-route-schema=v2` so we can gate strict behavior 3) console show a small banner in the UI when route attr mismatch count > 0.
aj: +1. Also add rollout exit criteria: don't flip strict mode for prod until `route_schema_v2_ratio >= 0.95` across traffic or shim present. we have metric `route_schema_v2_ratio` in the console already.
kevin: yep. i'll add the proxy shim and revert strict flag in prod until shim lands. will open a PR.
julie: support: i've opened a ticket and notified L2. any quick mitigation for embedders? perhaps SDK patches that fallback to raw header on 400 with message 'route-schema-mismatch'?
maria: SDKs can do a tiny fallback: if server responds 400/422 with `route-schema-mismatch`, resend with `x-rd-route-raw` populated. cut patch for py/ts/go today.
aj: timeline? we should aim for hotfix before EOD.
kevin: proxy shim deployed to canary. deploy-bot: canary 6101020333 rolled.
deploy-bot: canary 6101020333 succeeded in us-west and eu-west, monitoring for 15m.
kevin: rolling to prod after 30m of healthy canary. reverting strict flag for prod in the meantime.
julie: thanks. can we document this in the console release notes and add a release checklist checkbox 'SDK opt-in + schema survey' so we don't surprise customers next time?
maria: yes — i'll write a short RFC and add the checklist. i'll own the SDK patches (assigning to myself).
aj: i'll update the console rollout automation to block strict flips until the metric threshold is met.
julie: great. i'll cross-post to product and support. closing thread once patches and canary are green. :thumbsup:
